title: GTN-Path: Efficient Path Timing Prediction through Waveform Propagation with Graph Transformer
problem: Static timing analysis (STA) must balance accuracy and runtime at advanced nodes; graph-based analysis (GBA) is fast but pessimistic; path-based analysis (PBA) is accurate but expensive. LUT-based standard cell libraries introduce accuracy losses vs. SPICE at advanced nodes, making sign-off STA unreliable.
motivation: As technology shrinks, LUT-based STA loses fidelity vs. SPICE, requiring more accurate but faster timing prediction methods for design closure.
method: The approach treats a circuit as a graph (network of connected logic components and wires) and uses a graph transformer network—an AI model trained to learn structural relationships—to predict how electrical signals propagate through it. It learns these predictions from accurate but expensive SPICE simulations, capturing waveforms (signal shapes over time) and timing delays. The model achieves ~3% error compared to SPICE while running 3510× faster.
key_novelty: A graph transformer network learns to predict electrical signal propagation directly, replacing lookup-table timing methods with a structural model that maintains simulation accuracy at advanced chip nodes.
contributions: GTN for post-layout path timing prediction via waveform propagation
Graph-based modeling of standard cells and interconnects
2.96–2.98% error vs. SPICE; 3510× speedup vs. HSPICE
12× speedup vs. commercial sign-off STA tools
limitations: Evaluation on specific technology node not detailed; generalization to sub-5nm or beyond; handling of cross-die/multi-die timing; accuracy on highly congested designs not discussed.
primary_theme: graph transformer waveform propagation for accurate post-layout timing prediction
